parent_objective: design fresh fixed-budget L0/L1/L2/L3 profile refresh after artifact inventory finds old profile checkpoints incompatible with M1362 architecture ranking
blocked_by: M1383 blocks direct M1212-vs-M1362 architecture ranking and requires a fresh fixed-budget refresh design
supersedes: direct comparison of old M1212 checkpoints against M1362
running profile training without fixed budget and gate policy
using M1362 as fixed-budget architecture checkpoint

public_gates: M1384 must design the fresh fixed-budget profile refresh before training
M1384 must preserve current-tiled L2 and corrected L3 reset controls
M1384 must define training seeds, budgets, evaluation seeds, gate order, and claim boundaries
M1384 must keep M1362 as diagnostic anchor rather than architecture-ranking checkpoint
forbidden_shortcuts: do not compare old and new checkpoints as fair architecture ranking
do not drop current-tiled L2 controls
do not drop corrected L3 reset-control
do not claim paper-level profile ranking

workflow_synthesis.evidence_increment: designs fresh fixed-budget profile refresh required for fair architecture comparison after artifact inventory
workflow_synthesis.claim_scope: design only; no training, new evaluation, PPO, promotion, private holdout, high-fidelity, profile-ranking, paper-level, or strong self-identification claim
stop_condition: stop if training budgets or seeds differ by profile without pre-registration
stop if current-tiled L2 controls are omitted
stop if corrected L3 reset-control is omitted
stop if M1362 is treated as a fixed-budget profile checkpoint
fallback_plan: if fixed-budget refresh is too large, route to a smaller smoke with the same profile set
if config generation is stale, route to current-profile config generator update
if evaluation runner is stale, route to profile runner update before training
if public source-rich diagnostics cannot be integrated, keep them secondary and run standard public comparison first

admission_evidence: M1383 finds M1362 lacks profile metadata and is not fixed-budget comparable to M1212
M1382 defines comparison protocol and required controls
allowed_updates: status, queue, scoreboard, research log, and review
next_stage_criteria: fixed training and eval budgets are specified
gate and metric ordering is specified
next config-generation or smoke route is explicit

self_id_evidence_discipline.current_frame_substitution_risk: M1384 must keep L0/L1 and current-tiled L2 controls in the design so later comparisons can separate current-frame substitution from history.
history_necessity_tests: include L3 zero-action and zero-response diagnostics where compatible
keep source-rich temporal diagnostics secondary until seed diversity improves
self_id_evidence_discipline.temporal_evidence_window: M1382-M1383 profile comparison protocol and inventory.
self_id_evidence_discipline.negative_result_policy: If a fair fixed-budget design cannot be specified, route to profile-runner/config repair instead of training.
allowed_claims: fixed-budget profile refresh design and next route
no promotion, corpus export, training, PPO, private-holdout, high-fidelity, paper-level profile ranking, or level3 self-identification claim

hypothesis: A fresh fixed-budget L0/L1/L2/L3 profile refresh can be designed so later runs produce fair public architecture evidence rather than lineage-confounded comparisons.
success_criteria: design specifies profile set and required controls
design specifies fixed training seeds, budgets, and eval seeds
design specifies gate order and claim boundaries
design chooses next config-generation or smoke route without training, PPO, promotion, private holdout, corpus export, or actor-input expansion
failure_criteria: design treats M1362 as a fixed-budget architecture checkpoint
design routes directly to training, PPO, promotion, private holdout, corpus export, or source-rich expansion without config/runtime checks
decision_rule: M1384 passes if it designs a fresh fixed-budget profile refresh and next config/runtime route before any training, new evaluation, PPO, promotion, private holdout, corpus export, or actor-input expansion.
